thread:
kevin: Quick heads-up: started seeing a 5-12ms p50 regression on small-batch decode after toggling FlashPaged->FlashFused on a subset of GPUs. Anyone else noticing this? :thinking_face:

maria: Saw the same at ~09:12 PT. p99 also crept up. This looks specific to decode paths — prefill steady.

sophia: Can you paste a perf profile? Curious if it's kernel launch overhead or memory copy churn with the paged layout.

kevin: Profiling snippet from devbox (continuous batching enabled):
```
GPU kernel samples:
  flash_fused_attn_small           42%
  flash_paged_attn                 18%
  kv_cache_lookup                  12%
  contiguous_matmul                8%
  cudaMemcpyAsync                  6%
  scheduler_wait                   5%
```
Note the fused kernel dominates samples during decode spikes; prefill still uses flash_paged_attn and is fine.

maria: Hmm, I also saw the KV cache miss rate jump ~14% for these requests which would increase memcpy and force extra re-materialization. Could be interaction between paged attention tiled layout and our decode K/V stride.

kevin: I ran a micro-bench: small-batch decode (batch sizes 1-4, seq_len=8..64). Results:
```
case: batch=1, seq=32 -> flash_fused p50=18.2ms, flash_paged p50=11.3ms
case: batch=2, seq=32 -> flash_fused p50=13.0ms, flash_paged p50=9.8ms
case: batch=4, seq=128 -> flash_fused p50=10.1ms, flash_paged p50=10.9ms
```
So fused helps at larger seqs/batches but regresses for tiny decode windows. Launch and occupancy matter.

alan: Sounds like batching heuristics and kernel selection interplay. Our continuous batcher can fold inflight decodes into micro-batches; if the runtime then picks flash_fused because aggregate seq looks larger, but per-request seq is small, tail tasks suffer. We might need per-request cost estimates instead of aggregate-only decisions.

ci-bot: A/B job started: run/attn-smalldecode-abtest-2187654321 on 20 GPUs (10% traffic)

sophia: I pushed a quick runtime tweak on a branch: if decode_op && max_seq_per_req <= 64 && effective_batch <= 4 -> prefer "small-decode" kernels (non-fused). Early Canary: p50 back to baseline, p99 reduced 30%.

kevin: Nice. Also noticed KV cache eviction stride causes extra page remaps for paged_attention when sequences are short and interleaved. We should add per-request KV hit metric to decision logic.

maria: I'll add tracepoints for kv_hit_rate/token and a lightweight ascii histogram in the debug path. Then we can feed that to the cost model: approximate_cost = alpha*kernel_latency + beta*(1-kv_hit_rate)*mem_copy_cost.

kevin: Sounds good. Can we gate the change with a rollout flag so we can rollback quickly? If the A/B looks good, we should bake heuristic for next release.

sophia: Yep — using rollout flag "small_decode_kernel_pref". ci-bot scheduled 6hr canary, will auto-roll if error rate < 1% and latency delta < +2ms.

maria: Created issue #6521 with notes and perf artifacts, assigning to runtime-kernel-selection. cc @sophia @kevin

kevin: Great. Next steps: (1) instrument kv-hit metrics, (2) refine cost model, (3) add explicit rule for decode small-batches, (4) monitor A/B and iterate. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
